# Stellar guides for this project

These guides match the versions this project was generated with. Read the one for the area you are
changing before you change it.

- `contracts.md`: Contracts
- `networks.md`: Networks
- `outdated.md`: Outdated patterns

Examples use `npm run`. With another package manager, use its own form, such as `pnpm setup`.

For the Stellar CLI's own guide for agents, run `stellar skill`. Check `stellar <command> --help`
before using a flag. Configuration is in `.env`; `.env.example` lists every key.
---OUTDATED---
# Outdated patterns

Stellar tooling changed quickly, and older examples (and older training data) use patterns that no
longer work or are deprecated. Use the right-hand column instead.

| Outdated | Use instead | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `stellar contract bindings typescript` | `npx @stellar/stellar-sdk generate` (here: the contracts:bindings script) | https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/stellar-cli#stellar-contract-bindings-typescript |
| `@stellar/stellar-base` | `@stellar/stellar-sdk`, which includes it (also as `@stellar/stellar-sdk/base`) | installed: npm marks `@stellar/stellar-base` 15.0.0 deprecated, "rolled into @stellar/stellar-sdk" |
| `SorobanRpc.Server` | `rpc.Server` from `@stellar/stellar-sdk` | installed: `@stellar/stellar-sdk` 17.4.0 exports `rpc` and no `SorobanRpc` |
| `soroban` CLI commands, such as `soroban contract build` | The same commands under `stellar`, such as `stellar contract build` | https://developers.stellar.org/docs/networks/software-versions |
| `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target | `wasm32v1-none` (Rust 1.84 or newer), through `stellar contract build` | https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/rust-dialect#limited-webassembly-features |
| `cargo build --target wasm32v1-none` for contracts | `stellar contract build`, which applies the settings the network needs | https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/smart-contracts/getting-started/hello-world#build-the-contract |
| `@stellar/freighter-api` | `@stellar/varial-sdk` (Freighter is now Varial) | https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/guides/freighter/prompt-to-sign-tx |
| `stellar fee-stats` | `stellar fees stats` | installed: Stellar CLI 30.0.1 marks `fee-stats` deprecated |

Soroban-RPC is now called Stellar RPC (renamed in November 2024,
https://developers.stellar.org/docs/data/apis/rpc). It is the same service.
---CONTRACTS---
# Agent instructions

This is a Stellar smart-contract workspace (Soroban). Each contract is a workspace member under `contracts/<name>/`.

## Layout

- `Cargo.toml` — workspace root; contract crates inherit `soroban-sdk` from here
- `contracts/<name>/src/lib.rs` — contract implementation (`#![no_std]`)
- `contracts/<name>/src/test.rs` — host-side unit tests

## Build

From the workspace root:

```sh
stellar contract build
```

That compiles every `cdylib` member to WASM. Artifacts land in `target/wasm32v1-none/release/*.wasm`. Build one crate with `stellar contract build --package <name>`.

Do not substitute this with `cargo build --target wasm32v1-none`. `stellar contract build` applies the flags and metadata the network expects.

The `wasm32v1-none` Rust target must be installed (`rustup target add wasm32v1-none`). Rust 1.84 or newer is required for that target. Rust 1.82 and 1.83 cannot build contracts.

## Test

Host tests run with the normal Cargo test harness (not on-chain):

```sh
cargo test
```

A single crate: `cargo test -p <name>`.

## Deploy and invoke

On testnet, after a successful build:

```sh
stellar contract deploy \
  --wasm target/wasm32v1-none/release/<name>.wasm \
  --source-account <identity> \
  --network testnet \
  --alias <alias>

stellar contract invoke \
  --id <alias> \
  --network testnet \
  --source-account <identity> \
  -- hello --to world
```

The sample `hello_world` contract exposes `hello(to: String) -> Vec<String>`. Replace that with your own functions; `stellar contract invoke --id <id> -- -h` prints the generated CLI for the deployed contract.

## Further reading

- https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/smart-contracts/overview
- https://github.com/stellar/soroban-examples

# Stellar CLI skill

A guide for AI agents driving the `stellar` CLI. Follow these conventions so commands stay short, reproducible, and free of hard-coded secrets and ids.

## Overview

The Stellar CLI (`stellar`) manages keys and accounts, builds and deploys smart contracts, deploys asset contracts, streams events, and encodes/decodes XDR.

- Every command has help: `stellar <command> --help`.
- List a contract's functions and their arguments on the fly:

      stellar contract invoke --id <contract> -- --help

  Anything after `--` is parsed against the contract's own schema.

## Networks: prefer `stellar network use`

Set a default network once instead of repeating `--network`, `--rpc-url`, and `--network-passphrase` on every command:

    stellar network use testnet

After this, other commands use that network by default and you can omit the network flags entirely.

- List configured networks: `stellar network ls`
- Add a custom network: `stellar network add <name> --rpc-url <url> --network-passphrase <passphrase>`
- Clear the default: `stellar network unset`

Only pass `--network <name>` explicitly when a single command needs to target a different network than the default.

## Identities: prefer `stellar keys use`, never raw secret keys

Create named identities and select a default with `stellar keys use`, just like networks. Do not paste raw `S...` secret seeds on the command line.

    stellar keys generate alice --fund   # generates and funds on testnet
    stellar keys use alice               # sign and pay as alice by default

After `stellar keys use`, other commands sign and pay with that identity, so you can omit the source flag entirely.

- List identities: `stellar keys ls`
- Show an address: `stellar keys address alice`

content.text:
Everything is built, deployed and checked except one thing: I could not exercise the wallet connect and sign flow in a browser.

## What I built

- **Contract** `contracts/contracts/staking` (crate `staking`). The constructor takes the token address; `constructor.json` sets it to `asset:native`, so the contract is usable as soon as it is deployed.
  - `stake(user, amount)` requires `user`'s auth, transfers `amount` from the user into the contract, and credits the user.
  - `unstake(user, amount)` requires auth and fails with `InsufficientStake` if the user has less than `amount` staked. Otherwise it transfers the amount back.
  - `staked(user)` and `total_staked()` return the balances as `i128`.
  - Amounts must be positive. Non-positive amounts fail with `InvalidAmount`.
- **Unit tests**: 9 in `test.rs`, covering staking, multiple users, partial and full unstaking, unstaking more than staked (both the panic and the non-panicking `try_` path, which also checks nothing changed), unstaking with no stake, and invalid amounts.
- **Testnet deployment**: contract `CB4MZSH5HV5E2TCI2O7U6XNBOGI56ESBYKL2ZSSDMTK6WA2N3LI7KUPZ`, alias `staking-app-staking`. `deployment.txt` contains only that ID, with no trailing newline.
- **Page** `/staking` (`app/staking/`):
  - The total is read on the server from the contract and rendered as a bare integer in `data-testid="total-staked"`.
  - `connect-wallet` calls `requestAccess()` from `@stellar/varial-sdk` 7.0.0. The docs say Varial replaces Freighter, and I pinned the version.
  - The form (`stake-amount`, `stake-submit`) signs with the connected wallet and calls `stake`, then `router.refresh()` to update the total.
- **Generated client**: `packages/staking` and `lib/contracts.ts` gained a `staking()` export. I did not edit `packages/`.

## Choices I made

- The stake input takes **stroops** (integer; 1 XLM = 10000000), to match the raw integer the total shows.
- The `hello_world` sample contract is still in the workspace and deployed, and the root page still uses it.

## How I verified it

- `npm run check` passes: typecheck, lint, all contract tests (10, including 9 staking), and `next build`. `/staking` is in the route list.
- `npm run setup` created and funded the `dev` identity on testnet, built, deployed and generated bindings.
- On-chain, via the CLI: `total_staked` returned `0`, a 1 XLM `stake` moved it to `10000000`, and `unstake` brought it back to `0`.
- I served the production build and fetched `/staking`. It shows `total-staked` = `0` from testnet and includes the connect button and both form controls.
- The generated client's `stake` call simulates successfully for the `dev` address.
- I scanned the tree for secret-key patterns and found none.

## Not verified

- **Wallet flow.** I did not run connect and sign in a browser because no Varial or Freighter extension is available here. The button and form are verified only as rendered HTML and by the simulated call above, not by a real signature.
- `npm audit` reported vulnerabilities after installing the wallet SDK. I did not address them.
- Nothing is committed. `contracts/**/test_snapshots/` and `contracts/Cargo.lock` were generated by the test runs.

RESULT: FAIL: the wallet connect and sign flow in a real browser was not exercised; everything else is verified.
